fr.modeOffline: Mode hors ligne : analyse locale uniquement
fr.cautionBody: Valeur fictive affichée sur 1.00. Ce n’est ni une probabilité ni un niveau de confiance ; elle invite seulement à examiner les preuves avec prudence.
fr.insufficientBody: Les observations fictives fournies ne permettent pas de retenir une hypothèse. Aucune conclusion n’est proposée.
fr.conflictItem: Ces observations fictives se contredisent. Vérifiez chaque source avant toute interprétation.
fr.safetyReview: Examen humain requis (HUMAN_REVIEW) : en cas de contradiction, arrêtez l’interprétation automatique et faites examiner les sources par une personne.
fr.safetyNotice: Démo éducative fictive. Ne l’utilisez pas pour décider d’une action réelle.
fr.remoteNotesBody: Section facultative, désactivée par défaut. Ces notes ne font pas partie du graphe ni des hypothèses de référence de la démo.
fr.remoteNoteStatus: Note non vérifiée — ne vaut pas seconde source
fr.remoteCitations: Références fictives mentionnées dans la note
fr.sourceServerTrace: Source : trace du serveur de démonstration
fr.cautionUpdate: Indice de prudence : de {before} à {after} (illustratif, non probabiliste)

ar.modeOffline: الوضع غير المتصل: تحليل محلي فقط
ar.modeRemoteAccepted: تم استلام ملاحظة عن بُعد، غير مُتحقَّق منها
ar.modeRemoteRejected: رُفضت الملاحظة عن بُعد ولم تُستخدم
ar.cautionBody: قيمة خيالية معروضة من أصل 1.00. ليست احتمالًا ولا مستوى ثقة؛ بل تنبّه فقط إلى ضرورة الحذر عند مراجعة الأدلة.
ar.insufficientBody: لا تسمح الملاحظات الخيالية المقدَّمة باعتماد أي فرضية. لا يُقترح أي استنتاج.
ar.verificationUnverified: غير مُتحقَّق منه — مصدر خيالي واحد
ar.conflictItem: تتعارض هذه الملاحظات الخيالية. راجع كل مصدر قبل أي تفسير.
ar.safetyReview: يلزم فحص بشري (HUMAN_REVIEW): عند وجود تعارض، أوقف التفسير التلقائي واطلب من شخص مراجعة المصادر.
ar.safetyNotice: عرض تعليمي خيالي. لا تستخدمه لاتخاذ قرار بشأن إجراء حقيقي.

placeholderRules.addedIds: ar: render every ID inside {ids} separately with an LTR isolate element (for example <bdi>) created via textContent, keeping DOM order exactly as supplied. Latin letters plus digits are weak-directional and adjacent Arabic punctuation can visually reorder or attach to the wrong ID. fr: keep the same DOM order; isolation is harmless.
placeholderRules.removedIds: ar: render every ID inside {ids} separately with an LTR isolate element via textContent, keeping supplied DOM order and the removed/inactive meaning of the label. Isolation prevents e1/e2 from swapping visually or appearing attached to the wrong Arabic word. Never reuse the added-IDs list or styling that implies activity.
placeholderRules.newFindingsCount: ar: render {count} as one LTR-isolated numeric token via textContent. Digits are weak-directional beside Arabic text and could be read or displayed next to the wrong phrase. fr: keep {count} as a plain text node in the same position.
placeholderRules.withdrawnFindingsCount: ar: render {count} as one LTR-isolated numeric token via textContent, for the same weak-direction reason as other numbers. The surrounding label must stay visibly and semantically about withdrawn, inactive hypotheses. fr: keep {count} as a plain text node.
placeholderRules.conflictDelta: ar: render {delta}, including any leading sign supplied by code, as one LTR-isolated token via textContent. A sign and digits can detach or reverse beside Arabic punctuation, changing increase into apparent decrease. fr: preserve the signed value exactly as supplied.
placeholderRules.cautionUpdate: ar: render {before} and {after} each as a separate LTR-isolated numeric token via textContent, in that DOM order. Separate isolation stops the two decimal values from swapping around the Arabic words for from/to. fr: keep before then after in the same order. In both locales, build nodes with textContent only, never innerHTML, and add no bidi control characters to the translation string.

accessibilityAudit: 360px real-device check: set ar and fr at 360 CSS px wide; results, safety text, change summary and relation cards reflow with no horizontal scrolling, clipped IDs, or truncated buttons. Fail if any content requires sideways panning.

200% zoom check: zoom to 200% and repeat analysis, conflict and remote-note states; all text remains readable, focus is not hidden under sticky headings, and the HUMAN_REVIEW safety copy remains fully reachable. Fail if content overlaps or disappears.

Keyboard check: tab through language switch, analyze button, results, safety section and remote-notes disclosure in a logical order; activate controls with Enter/Space and see a clear focus indicator. Fail on keyboard traps, graph-only access, or focus loss after analyzeBusy changes to results.

Screen-reader check: use aria-live polite for one concise summary only, such as state, counts and cautionUpdate; do not announce every graph edge. Headings must separate findingsTitle from remoteNotesTitle. Fail if the live region repeats the full graph, reads remote notes as findings, or announces busy repeatedly.

RTL/LTR check: in ar, page direction is RTL while every e1/e2 ID, HUMAN_REVIEW, count, delta and caution value stays LTR-isolated and in supplied DOM order. Fail if punctuation jumps, e2 appears before e1 when e1 was supplied first, or numbers swap in cautionUpdate.

Meaning-not-color check: conflict, unverified and withdrawn states are conveyed by text labels, not color, icons, meters or position alone; caution has no progressbar role and no percent sign. Fail if removing color makes HUMAN_REVIEW, verificationUnverified or withdrawn status ambiguous.

testCases.input: Offline, ar, addedIds receives e1 then e2.
testCases.expected: Change panel shows addedIds in Arabic with e1 and e2 each LTR-isolated and in supplied DOM order; screen reader reads e1 before e2.
testCases.failCondition: Fail if e2 is read or displayed as the first supplied item, IDs merge with Arabic punctuation, or raw bidi controls appear in the string.

testCases.input: Offline, ar, removedIds receives e2 then e1, deliberately unsorted.
testCases.expected: Removed list preserves e2 then e1 exactly as supplied and is labelled as removed, not active.
testCases.failCondition: Fail if code sorts to e1,e2, reverses the list, or styles the removed IDs as current evidence.

testCases.input: Offline, ar, one update adds e1 and removes e2.
testCases.expected: addedIds and removedIds appear as separate labelled lines; e1 is only under added and e2 only under removed.
testCases.failCondition: Fail if e1/e2 cross between lines, either ID loses LTR isolation, or the removed e2 is announced as newly available.

testCases.input: Offline, ar, analysis completes after e1 and e2 are selected, with several fictional graph relations present.
testCases.expected: aria-live gives one concise result summary with state and counts; it does not read every edge or repeat e1/e2 for each relation.
testCases.failCondition: Fail if the live region enumerates all edges, repeats the summary, or orders the cited IDs differently from the supplied e1,e2 order.

testCases.input: Offline, Meta adapter enabled by explicit user action; one metaAnnotations item cites two fictional references and mentions e1,e2.
testCases.expected: Item appears only under remoteNotesTitle with remoteNoteStatus and remoteCitations; it is outside findingsTitle, outside the canonical graph edges, and keeps verificationUnverified.
testCases.failCondition: Fail if the note is grouped with h-flow or h-intermittent, added as a graph edge, counted as a second source, or changes any verification label to verified.

testCases.input: Offline, remote note is accepted by transport, then a second identical remote note arrives.
testCases.expected: modeRemoteAccepted may be shown, but both items remain unverified remote notes and do not corroborate each other.
testCases.failCondition: Fail if duplication upgrades status, removes remoteNoteStatus, creates a canonical hypothesis, or implies independent verification.

testCases.input: Offline, fictional e3 and e4 contradict each other and a provisional hypothesis exists.
testCases.expected: conflictTitle, conflictItem and the global safetyReview HUMAN_REVIEW copy dominate above provisional findings; no actionable conclusion is presented.
testCases.failCondition: Fail if a hypothesis is presented as settled, the safety copy is hidden below a dismissible note, or conflict is conveyed by color alone.

testCases.input: Offline, HUMAN_REVIEW is active and then an unverified remote note is received.
testCases.expected: HUMAN_REVIEW remains visible and dominant; the remote note stays in its separate section and cannot clear or soften the conflict state.
testCases.failCondition: Fail if receiving the note removes safetyReview, marks the conflict resolved, or moves focus away from the safety message without user action.

testCases.input: Offline, fictional caution value is displayed as 0.87 / 1.00 beside cautionTitle and cautionBody.
testCases.expected: Text explicitly says the illustrative value is neither a probability nor a confidence level; no percent sign, confidence meter or progressbar semantics are used.
testCases.failCondition: Fail if 87, a percent sign, a meter, or wording such as confidence, accuracy or likely correctness appears.

testCases.input: Offline, cautionUpdate receives before 0.40 and after 0.65 in fr and ar.
testCases.expected: Both locales announce from 0.40 to 0.65 in that order with illustrative, non-probabilistic wording; ar isolates each number.
testCases.failCondition: Fail if values swap, the update is phrased as increased certainty or correctness, or a percent conversion is added.

testCases.input: Offline, only fictional e1 is supplied and no hypothesis meets the demo rule.
testCases.expected: insufficientTitle and insufficientBody appear; findings list is empty and no diagnosis or conclusion is suggested.
testCases.failCondition: Fail if h-flow, h-intermittent or any other hypothesis is shown as active or recommended.

testCases.input: Offline, an update withdraws one previously provisional hypothesis and adds none.
testCases.expected: withdrawnFindingsCount counts it as withdrawn and inactive; it disappears from active findings and remains only in the change history.
testCases.failCondition: Fail if the withdrawn hypothesis remains under findingsTitle, is announced as new, or can be selected as a current result.

rejectedWording.misleading: Diagnostic confirmé avec une confiance de 87 %
rejectedWording.improved: Hypothèse provisoire non vérifiée ; indice de prudence illustratif affiché sur 1.00
rejectedWording.reason: The misleading version invents a diagnosis and a calibrated percentage; the improved version keeps the fictional, unverified and non-probabilistic boundaries.

rejectedWording.misleading: Note distante vérifiée par une seconde source
rejectedWording.improved: Note distante non vérifiée — ne vaut pas seconde source
rejectedWording.reason: Transport acceptance is not verification, and a remote note never corroborates the canonical evidence.

rejectedWording.misleading: L’hypothèse retirée reste disponible dans les résultats
rejectedWording.reason: Withdrawn explanations must not look selectable, current or semantically active.

rejectedWording.misleading: Aucun conflit : vous pouvez conclure en toute sécurité
rejectedWording.improved: En cas de contradiction, examen humain requis ; aucune conclusion automatique
rejectedWording.reason: The misleading version guarantees safety and correctness; the improved version preserves HUMAN_REVIEW dominance.

rejectedWording.improved: Note distante facultative, hors hypothèses et hors graphe
rejectedWording.reason: metaAnnotations are separate unverified notes, never canonical hypotheses or graph edges.

rejectedWording.misleading: Indice de confiance en hausse, résultat plus probable
rejectedWording.improved: Indice de prudence illustratif : de {before} à {after}, non probabiliste
rejectedWording.reason: A caution-score change is not a change in probability, confidence or correctness.

implementationNotes: Stage 1: add fr and ar dictionaries beside the existing language data, keyed exactly as specified; fall back to the existing language only for a missing UI string outside this pack, and log no user data.

Stage 2: render all strings with textContent. For placeholders, split only on the exact tokens {ids}, {count}, {delta}, {before} and {after}; create <bdi> elements for IDs and numbers under ar, set their textContent, and append nodes in supplied order. Never use innerHTML and never add bidi control characters to stored strings.

Stage 3: keep three separate DOM regions with separate headings: canonical findings, change summary, and metaAnnotations under remoteNotesTitle. Do not move remote-note nodes into findings or graph-edge lists, and keep the Meta adapter off unless the user explicitly enables it.

Stage 4: apply precedence in plain JavaScript: if a conflict exists, render safetyReview in the global safety region before findings and keep it visible regardless of remote-note or caution updates; withdrawn IDs and hypotheses get inactive labels and are removed from active lists.

Stage 5: use one polite aria-live summary for completion, busy and concise updates; update analyzeButton disabled state and analyzeBusy text without moving focus unexpectedly. At 700px and below keep relation cards, and test at 360px, 200% zoom, keyboard only, a screen reader, and ar LTR isolation before release.
